title: Indian Contract Act, 1872 — Section 135 (Discharge of surety when creditor compounds with, gives time to, or agrees not to sue, principal debtor)

content.overview: Section 135 provides that a contract between the creditor and the principal debtor, by which the creditor makes a composition with, or promises to give time to, or not to sue, the principal debtor, discharges the surety, unless the surety assents to such contract.
content.glance: Composition, promise of time, or agreement not to sue the principal debtor discharges the surety unless the surety assents.
content.study: A contract between the creditor and the principal debtor, by which the creditor makes a composition with, or promises to give time to, or not to sue, the principal debtor, discharges the surety, unless the surety assents to such contract. Identify the contract with the principal debtor, the composition/time/non-sue term, and absence of the surety's assent. Current-law framing: assent by the surety preserves liability; mere forbearance without a binding agreement is addressed in Section 137.

sections.heading: Core rule
sections.body: A contract between the creditor and the principal debtor, by which the creditor makes a composition with, or promises to give time to, or not to sue, the principal debtor, discharges the surety, unless the surety assents to such contract.

sections.heading: Assent exception
sections.body: Discharge does not occur if the surety assents to the contract.

sections.heading: Distinction from forbearance
sections.body: Section 137 provides that mere forbearance to sue does not discharge the surety. Section 135 requires a contract (composition, promise of time, or agreement not to sue).

examples.title: Promise of time without assent
examples.body: The creditor promises the principal debtor further time to pay without the surety's assent. The surety is discharged under Section 135.

examples.title: Composition with assent
examples.body: The creditor compounds with the principal debtor and the surety assents. The surety remains liable.

hypotheticals.question: The creditor agrees with the principal debtor not to sue for six months, without the surety's assent. Is the surety discharged?
hypotheticals.analysis: Yes. Section 135 discharges the surety where the creditor contracts not to sue the principal debtor, unless the surety assents.

enhancement.detailedExplanation: Section 135 discharges the surety when the creditor contracts with the principal debtor to compound, give time, or not to sue, unless the surety assents. The provision requires a contract; mere forbearance without a binding agreement does not discharge under this section (see Section 137). Assent by the surety prevents discharge.
examples: Promise of further time without assent discharges the surety.
Assent by the surety to a composition preserves the surety's liability.
distinctions: Section 135 requires a contract with the principal debtor; Section 136 addresses an agreement with a third person to give time (which does not discharge).
Section 137 provides that mere forbearance does not discharge.
